findings.quote: Second-quarter sales were $5,187 million, up 3% reported and in line with that organically
findings.issue: The release's Table 2 gives Honeywell Technologies sales of $5,187 million, up 3% reported and organic growth of 4% — not 'in line with' the 3% reported. The report's own analystCommentary, thesis and finalRecommendation all say 4% organic, so the financials section contradicts both the release and the rest of the report at the one number the growth argument rests on.
findings.fix: Write 'up 3% reported and 4% organically', and keep the reported/organic wedge (currency, acquisitions, the PPE divestiture) as the explanation rather than collapsing the two figures.
findings.note: Fixed. incomeCommentary now reads 'up 3% reported and 4% organically', matching Table 2 of the release and the four other fields that say 4%.

findings.quote: with more than half of its sales outside the U.S., it faces tariffs and retaliatory tariffs, sanctions and trade barriers
findings.issue: The pack does not support 'sales outside the U.S.' above half. The FY25 geography split in the Facts block is United States 58.2%, Europe 21.7%, Other International 20.2% — non-U.S. is 41.8%. The 10-Q risk factor says something different: 'Our international operations, including U.S. exports, represent more than half of the Company's sales.' That is a different quantity, and the report quotes it correctly twice elsewhere (companyOverview: 'international operations remain more than half of sales'; risks[3]: 'international operations exceed half of sales') before restating it wrongly here.
findings.fix: Use the risk factor's own quantity — international operations including U.S. exports — rather than 'sales outside the U.S.', and note that the 58.2% U.S. geography split in the Facts block is a pre-spin FY25 figure measured on a different basis.
findings.note: Fixed. risks.systemic now reads 'with international operations, including U.S. exports, representing more than half of sales'. companyOverview goes further and flags that the 58.2% U.S. geography split measures a different quantity.

findings.quote: Consensus FY26E revenue of $20.1B and EPS of $8.32 sit inside guidance
findings.issue: FY26E consensus revenue of $20.1B does not sit inside guidance. Table 4 of the release puts current full-year sales guidance at $19.8B – $20.0B, so consensus sits above the top of the range. Only the EPS half of the sentence is true ($8.32 inside $8.05–$8.35), and the report states that correctly in multiplesCommentary.
findings.fix: Split the claim: consensus FY26E EPS of $8.32 sits inside the guided $8.05 to $8.35, while consensus FY26E revenue of $20.1B sits above the guided $19.8 billion to $20.0 billion — a gap worth a sentence, since the guidance was cut for divestiture timing the consensus mean may not yet carry.
findings.note: Fixed and split as suggested: EPS of $8.32 'sits inside the guided range' while revenue of $20.1B 'sits just above the sales guidance, which was trimmed for divestiture timing the consensus mean may not yet carry'.

findings.quote: Guidance went up on every line: 2026 adjusted EPS to $8.05 to $8.35, organic growth by a point at both ends, segment margin to 20.1% to 20.5%.
findings.issue: Guidance did not go up on every line. Table 4 shows sales guidance cut from $19.9B–$20.2B to $19.8B–$20.0B and both operating cash flow ($2.1B) and free cash flow ($2.0B) unchanged. The same overstatement appears in two more places: growth.points[0] ('Guidance moved up on every line on July 23, 2026', which then concedes in its own final clause that sales guidance is lower) and finalRecommendation.body[0] ('guidance raised on every line'). meta.subtitle's 'guidance raised' rests on the same claim.
findings.fix: Say guidance was raised on organic growth, segment margin and adjusted EPS, with sales guidance cut on divestiture timing and cash-flow guidance unchanged — which is also what the transcript claims ('raising our full-year outlook for organic growth, segment margin, and adjusted earnings per share'). Fix all three fields.
findings.note: Fixed in all three fields. analystCommentary and growth.points[0] now name the three lines raised and say the sales range was trimmed and cash-flow guidance unchanged; finalRecommendation reads 'its growth, margin and earnings guidance raised'. 'every line' appears nowhere.

findings.quote: the pack's headlines stop on July 2, 2026 with two upgrades and a price target of $263 from Deutsche Bank
findings.issue: Wrong date and wrong characterisation. The Daiwa and Deutsche Bank items are dated 2026-06-30, not July 2, and the report dates them correctly in multiplesCommentary ('were written on June 30, 2026'). There is one upgrade, not two — Daiwa upgraded to Outperform (the headline appears three times across PubT/Benzinga/The Fly), while Deutsche Bank 'Maintains Buy' and raised its target to $263. The July 2 headlines are a community-solar commercial-operation item and BMO initiating coverage on Honeywell Aerospace at $276, which is a different issuer.
findings.fix: State that the headline window ends 2026-07-02, that the last HON-specific broker actions are dated June 30 — one upgrade (Daiwa, target $255) and one maintained Buy with a raised target (Deutsche Bank, $263) — and that the July 2 items concern a solar project and a Honeywell Aerospace initiation.
findings.note: Fixed. risks.idiosyncratic[0] now dates the window to July 2, the broker actions to June 30, names one upgrade (Daiwa, $255) and Deutsche Bank maintaining Buy at $263, and says the July 2 items are a solar project and BMO's initiation on Honeywell Aerospace, 'a different issuer'.

findings.quote: The forward multiple is the one to argue over, and it is a premium multiple for an industrial
findings.issue: 'A premium multiple for an industrial' is a relative-valuation claim with nothing on the grounding surface to measure it against. The Facts block's multiples section is explicitly labelled 'company column; peers pending a peer data source' and the rendered table carries the note 'Peer multiples pending a peer data source.' The report's own thesis concedes the point in the opposite direction: the company is 'priced at a forward multiple the pack cannot benchmark against peers.'
findings.fix: Drop 'premium' or attach it to something on the page — for example, that 20.2x on FY27E is above the 7.8x trailing P/E the pack prints for the pre-spin conglomerate, or simply argue the multiple against management's own approximately $12 three-year adjusted EPS bridge without a peer comparison the pack cannot support.
findings.note: Fixed. multiplesCommentary now says peer multiples are pending 'so the forward multiple cannot be called rich or cheap against the group' and argues it against management's own approximately $12 bridge instead.

findings.quote: and the same logic will have applied to the Aerospace distribution after the proxy's date
findings.issue: An inference the proxy invites but does not make. The April 10, 2026 DEF 14A excerpt describes equitable conversion-ratio adjustments for the Solstice distribution only; it predates the June 29, 2026 Aerospace Spin-Off and says nothing about how unvested awards were treated in it, and no other source in the pack does either. The authoring contract is explicit that governance claims rest on the proxy excerpt and that the report should say what the pack does not carry rather than infer. The paragraph otherwise does this well, listing four things it makes no claim on.
findings.fix: Add the Aerospace equity treatment to the list of things the proxy does not show — the excerpt covers Solstice only and predates the Aerospace distribution — instead of projecting the Solstice mechanic forward.
findings.note: Fixed. The forward projection is gone; governance now lists 'nothing on how unvested awards were treated in the Aerospace distribution, which came after the proxy's date' among the things it makes no claim on.

findings.quote: of which Aerospace has been distributed to shareholders and most of Energy and Sustainability Solutions left as Solstice Advanced Materials on October 30, 2025
findings.issue: 'Most of' is a quantified claim the pack cannot support. Nothing on the grounding surface sizes UOP against Advanced Materials inside the FY25 Energy and Sustainability Solutions label ($3.1B, 8.4%). The report's own moat section states the relationship without the quantifier — 'The vendor's Energy and Sustainability Solutions label covered UOP and Advanced Materials; Advanced Materials left as Solstice Advanced Materials on October 30, 2025' — and that is as far as the sources go. The quarter's Process Automation and Technology sales of $1,679 million, which include UOP, cut against the implication that little of the label remains.
findings.fix: Say that Advanced Materials left as Solstice Advanced Materials on October 30, 2025 and that UOP moved into Process Automation and Technology, without asserting which was the larger part.
findings.note: Fixed. companyOverview now says Advanced Materials left as Solstice and UOP moved into Process Automation and Technology, with no claim about which was the larger part.

findings.quote: the shares keep roughly today's forward multiple on FY27E earnings plus a year of growth, which lands between the current price and the consensus target
findings.issue: The Base case is not anchored to anything the reader can reproduce from the page. Today's forward multiple on FY27E earnings is the ~20.2x on $9.99 the report quotes five times — which is the current price of $201.38, not $235. 'Plus a year of growth' is doing all the work and names no figure: there is no FY28E EPS on the grounding surface, and no multiple is given for the re-rating. Since Base carries 50% of the weight and the $215–$255 target range is built to bracket it, the whole calls structure rests on this one unstated step.
findings.fix: Anchor the Base case to a figure that is on the page: either a stated multiple applied to FY27E EPS of $9.99 (roughly 23.5x gets to $235), or management's approximately $12 three-year adjusted EPS bridge discounted back. State the multiple once, in this driver, and let scenarioCommentary refer back to it in words.
findings.note: Fixed and reproducible: the Base driver now states '24.2x NTM multiple they carry today as the market rolls forward to FY27E earnings, which is approximately $242', and impliedPrice moved 235 to 242. 24.2 x $9.99 = $241.76, both figures on the page. Recomputed calls remain coherent: weighted fair value $229.0, +13.7% vs $201.38 (BUY envelope), band $215-$255 brackets Base $242, probabilities sum to 1.

findings.quote: The three-year margin path: over 200 basis points from stranded-cost removal, portfolio actions and the aerospace trademark agreement, plus 60 basis points a year of operating expansion; the moat section carries the mechanism.
findings.issue: The same margin-path claim is made in five places, each time with the same two figures and the same three drivers: catalysts[3]; businessMoat.moatFactors[2] ('management expects over 200 basis points of margin expansion quickly from stranded-cost removal, portfolio actions in Industrial Automation and the aerospace trademark agreement, then 60 basis points a year'); growth.points[4] ('over 200 basis points of quick margin expansion and 60 basis points a year after that'); risks.idiosyncratic[2] ('the over 200 basis points of quick margin expansion'); finalRecommendation.body[0] ('over 200 basis points of expansion from stranded-cost removal and portfolio actions, then 60 basis points a year').
findings.fix: Argue the bridge once — moatFactors[2] is the right home, since that is where the counter about corporate costs on a smaller base sits. Keep catalysts[3] as a pointer without the figures, and have growth.points[4], risks.idiosyncratic[2] and the final recommendation refer back in words ('the quick margin bridge', 'the stranded-cost step').
findings.note: Fixed. '200 basis points' and '60 basis points' now appear once each, in moatFactors[2]. catalysts[3], growth.points[4], risks.idiosyncratic[2] and finalRecommendation.body[1] all refer back in words ('the margin bridge', 'the quick margin bridge', 'the quick step in the margin bridge').

findings.quote: The Bear case carries the same weight because the shares have already fallen to the bottom of their range on information the pack does not contain, and a report that cannot see the reason should not assume it is benign.
findings.issue: The reason the target sits below consensus, and the reason the Bear case carries a quarter of the weight, is argued three times in different words: analystCommentary ('That silence leads the risk section, and it is why the target range sits below consensus rather than on it'), this sentence, and risks.idiosyncratic[0] ('We treat the decline as unexplained rather than benign, which is why the Bear case carries a full quarter of the weight and the target range sits below consensus'). finalRecommendation.body[1] makes it a fourth time ('those three gaps are why the target range sits below the Street's $261.82 consensus'). The Bear probability is also stated twice inside scenarioCommentary alone — 'split the remainder evenly' and 'carries the same weight'.
findings.fix: Argue it once, in scenarioCommentary, where the weights are set. Let analystCommentary and the final recommendation point at it, and cut the causal clause from risks.idiosyncratic[0] so the risk bullet describes the gap rather than re-deriving the weighting.
findings.note: Fixed. The three reasons are argued once in thesis.body; analystCommentary ('for the three reasons the thesis sets out') and finalRecommendation ('those are the three gaps the thesis names') point at it, and the causal clause was cut from risks.idiosyncratic[0], which now ends 'We treat the decline as unexplained rather than benign.' The Bear weight is stated once, in scenarioCommentary.

findings.quote: yet management expects high-single-digit growth in the second half as energy projects resume, backlog converts and catalyst volumes rise. The counter is that the collection headwinds in the Middle East the CFO cited sit in the same segment's geography.
findings.issue: risks.idiosyncratic[1] makes the same claim in nearly the same words: 'guidance now rests on a second-half inflection to high-single-digit growth as energy projects resume and catalyst volumes rise ... the collection headwinds in the Middle East the CFO cited are the evidence against.' Both name the same mechanism, the same guided growth rate and the same counter-evidence, and both attribute it to the CFO. This is the paraphrase case the lint cannot catch.
findings.fix: Keep the mechanism and the Middle East collections counter in the risk bullet, where the segment's risk factor and the order/book-to-bill evidence already sit, and cut growth.points[2] back to the growth claim itself — the organic decline of 1% in the quarter against a guided second-half acceleration — pointing at the risk section for the counter.
findings.note: Fixed. growth.points[2] is cut back to the organic decline against the guided acceleration and points on ('the risk section carries the mechanism and the case against'); the mechanism and the Middle East collections counter now sit only in risks.idiosyncratic[1].

findings.quote: The counter is that corporate costs previously spread across Aerospace now sit on a smaller base, and operating margin was 12.8% in the quarter, well below the 19.0% segment margin.
findings.issue: risks.idiosyncratic[2] argues the identical point: 'operating margin of 12.8% sat well below segment margin of 19.0% because separation costs and corporate expense sit between them.' financials.incomeCommentary introduces the same pair a third time ('operating margin slipped 50 basis points to 12.8% on separation costs below the segment line' alongside segment margin of 19.0%). Three fields carry the same two figures making the same argument about the gap between them.
findings.fix: Introduce the 12.8% / 19.0% gap once, in incomeCommentary, where the separation costs are quantified. Have the moat factor refer back in words ('the gap between segment and operating margin') and let risks.idiosyncratic[2] keep it, since the stranded-cost risk is its subject — but not both.
findings.note: Fixed. '12.8%' now appears once, in incomeCommentary. moatFactors[2] refers back ('the gap between segment and operating margin the financials section quantifies') and risks.idiosyncratic[2] keeps the argument without the figures.

findings.quote: Orders rose 13% led by data center and hospitality verticals, where management put orders growth at over 50% and sales growth at 30%
findings.issue: The 50%/30% figures are attached to the wrong quantity. The transcript says 'we drove over 50% orders growth and 30% organic sales growth in high-growth verticals', and names the focus verticals elsewhere as 'healthcare, hospitality, and data centers'. The release attributes only the 13% orders growth to data center and hospitality. Narrowing management's 'high-growth verticals' to the two the release names makes the report claim a growth rate for two verticals that the sources give for a wider group.
findings.fix: Write it as management does: orders rose 13%, led by data center and hospitality per the release, and management put orders growth above 50% and organic sales growth at 30% in its high-growth verticals, which it lists as healthcare, hospitality and data centers.
findings.note: Fixed as suggested: 'Orders rose 13%, led by data center and hospitality per the release; across what management calls its high-growth verticals, which it lists as healthcare, hospitality and data centers, it put orders growth above 50% and organic sales growth at 30%.'

findings.quote: tariffs and input costs keep gross margin below the 39.3% of a year earlier
findings.issue: 39.3% is the consolidated Q2 2025 gross margin — the old company, Aerospace included — as the MD&A gives it ('gross margin percentage decreased 170 basis points to 37.6% compared to 39.3% for the same period of 2025'), and incomeCommentary correctly labels it 'At the consolidated level'. The Bear case is a scenario for Honeywell Technologies, so the benchmark is the pre-spin conglomerate's. This is exactly the mixing the report's own thesis and financials section are built to prevent.
findings.fix: Anchor the Bear case to a Honeywell Technologies figure the pack carries — segment margin of 19.0% in the quarter, or the guided 20.1% to 20.5% for the year — rather than the consolidated gross margin; or keep 39.3% and say plainly that it is the consolidated figure and why it is still the relevant cost signal.
findings.note: Fixed. The Bear driver now reads 'push segment margin back below the quarter's 19.0% rather than toward the guided 20.1% to 20.5%'. The consolidated 39.3% no longer appears in the scenario.

findings.quote: with a 2.21% dividend yield that is calculated on pre-spin dividends
findings.issue: How the vendor computed the 2.21% is not on the grounding surface. The Facts block gives only 'Dividend Yield: 2.21%' and, in the Quote line, 'dividend yield 2.21%' as of 2026-09-14; nothing states the dividend rate behind it or the period it covers. The report's own capitalAllocation paragraph says 'the pack does not carry the standalone dividend policy', which is the honest version of the same observation.
findings.fix: Say what the pack shows: a 2.21% yield as of September 14, 2026 whose underlying dividend rate is not disclosed in the pack, and that the standalone post-spin dividend has not been set out — rather than asserting the basis of the vendor's calculation.
findings.note: Fixed. multiplesCommentary now reads 'a 2.21% dividend yield behind which no dividend rate is disclosed on this page', which is what the sources support.

findings.quote: An unexplained move: the shares sit near the bottom of their 52-week range and the pack carries no news after July 2, 2026; the risk section says what that does and does not tell us.
findings.issue: 'Near the bottom of the 52-week range' is asserted in eight fields: this bullet, analystCommentary, thesis.body, multiplesCommentary, scenarioCommentary, capitalAllocation, risks.idiosyncratic[0] and finalRecommendation.body[1]. The executive-summary pointer and the risk section that argues it are both appropriate; the other six are restatement, and they crowd out the one thing a reader can check — the report's own price history, which shows the fall running from about $246 in early August to $201.38 on September 14.
findings.fix: Keep the claim in this pointer and in risks.idiosyncratic[0], where it is argued against the headline window. Elsewhere refer back in words ('the decline described in the risk section'). Consider using the rendered price history to date the fall, which would sharpen the point that it began after the pack's headline window closed.
findings.note: Fixed. '52-week' is down from eight fields to four: meta.subtitle, analystCommentary, the executive-summary pointer and risks.idiosyncratic[0] where it is argued, plus multiplesCommentary which now only states the range rather than the position in it. thesis.body, scenarioCommentary and finalRecommendation.body[1] no longer assert it.

findings.quote: and we say plainly what the pack does not contain
findings.issue: 'The pack' is a tic: it appears 25 times across 16 fields — analystCommentary (2), thesis.body (4), risks[0], balanceCommentary (2), cashflowCommentary, multiplesCommentary, scenarioCommentary, moatFactors[3], durability, leadership (2), capitalAllocation (2), governance, insiderOwnership, risks.idiosyncratic[0] (3), risks.idiosyncratic[4] and finalRecommendation.body[0]. The honesty about what is not disclosed is the right instinct and the reason the report works; the single phrase carrying it every time is past the point of notice, and it also puts the desk's internal vocabulary in front of the reader.
findings.fix: Vary it and name the source when there is one — 'the 10-Q does not show', 'the proxy predates it', 'no post-spin balance sheet has been filed', 'nothing captured since July 2'. Keep 'the pack' for the two or three places where the absence of a source is itself the point.
findings.note: Fixed as asked: 'the pack' appears zero times, replaced by varied and source-named phrasing ('nothing captured after July 2', 'the second-quarter balance sheet is not among the captured excerpts', 'no post-spin balance sheet has been filed', 'in anything filed so far'). See F-20 for the residual pattern in the replacements.

findings.quote: The counter-case is a company whose guided free cash flow of $2.0B is a fraction of the conglomerate's, priced at a forward multiple the pack cannot benchmark against peers.
findings.issue: Four fields sit close enough to their caps that the fixes above have little room: thesis.body 1320/1500 (88%), incomeCommentary 2163/2500 (87%), companyOverview 2142/2500 (86%) and capitalAllocation 1267/1500 (84%). Several Critical fixes — the organic growth correction in incomeCommentary, dropping 'most of' in companyOverview — add words rather than remove them.
findings.fix: Recover space by cutting the repeated material named in F-10 through F-13 and F-17 before the fix round adds the corrections; the duplicated margin-path, 12.8%/19.0% and 52-week-range sentences are the cheapest to give back.
findings.note: The condition is cleared: every Critical and Important fix landed and every field is inside its cap. Three of the four named fields got shorter (thesis.body 88% to 85%, incomeCommentary 87% to 82%, capitalAllocation 84% to 83%). companyOverview went the other way, 86% to 91%, because it absorbed two Critical fixes. See F-21.

findings.quote: almost every trailing figure on this page describes the old company
findings.issue: The replacement for 'the pack' has settled into two stock phrases doing the same job. 'On this page' appears seven times across six fields — analystCommentary, thesis.body (twice), multiplesCommentary, moatFactors[3], risks.idiosyncratic[3] and finalRecommendation.body[0] — and 'captured' ten times across ten fields. Three of the seven are the same sentence rebuilt: this one, thesis.body's 'Every trailing multiple on this page, the 7.8x P/E', and finalRecommendation.body[0]'s 'The trailing figures on this page describe a company that no longer exists.' The volume of not-disclosed-here locutions is unchanged from round 1; only the vocabulary moved, and it has already begun to repeat.
findings.fix: Name the source or the absence directly where one exists — 'the vendor's snapshot', 'the FY25 tables', 'the 10-Q does not show', 'no post-spin balance sheet has been filed' — and reserve 'on this page' for the two or three places where what the reader can see rendered is itself the point. The trailing-figures claim is the report's thesis, so it can be stated once in analystCommentary and referred back to in the final recommendation rather than rebuilt a third time in thesis.body.

findings.quote: and it measures a different quantity from the 10-Q's statement that international operations, including U.S. exports, represent more than half of sales
findings.issue: companyOverview is now the tightest field on the page at 2277/2500 characters (91%), up from 86% in round 1, because it absorbed the F-2 and F-8 corrections. businessMoat.moatFactors[3] sits at 724/800 (90%), which is 76 characters of headroom, and moatFactors[2] at 690/800 (86%). Nothing material has been cut for space and every field is inside its cap, so this is a headroom observation rather than a breach — but these three fields have the least room left of anything on the page.
findings.fix: Recover headroom in companyOverview by moving the second paragraph's vendor-chart translation toward the moat section, which already maps each legacy label to what remains; the first and third paragraphs carry the company description and the current segment shape and are the parts the executive summary needs. In moatFactors[3], 'that no five-year series on this page describes the company that exists' restates what the thesis and the financials section already establish and can be cut to a clause.
